The generated `.dockerignore` for offload test sandboxes now explicitly re-includes the committed `.minds/template/*.sh` schemas: the docker-style matcher offload/Modal use does not honor `.gitignore`'s anchored `!/...` negations, so the templates were silently absent from sandbox images -- which broke the new deploy template-validation tests in CI. Operator secret directories under `.minds/<env>/` remain excluded.

A new meta-ratchet test (`test_generated_dockerignore_ships_all_committed_files` in the root `test_meta_ratchets.py`) now replicates the `_generate-dockerignore` transform and asserts, using Modal's real docker-style matcher, that no git-committed file is excluded by the generated `.dockerignore` -- so this class of silently-missing-from-sandbox-images bug fails at test time instead.

The dockerignore generation moved into `scripts/generate_dockerignore.sh` (called by the `_generate-dockerignore` recipe and exercised directly by the meta-ratchet test), and the script plus `.gitignore` are now offload `[checkpoint]` build inputs: the sandbox base image's `COPY` is filtered by the generated file, so ignore-rule changes must rebuild the checkpoint -- previously a stale checkpoint image silently kept dropping the template schemas even after the generation fix landed.
